ownership_reason: Only the gold sees each element together with the list's response to it and the position it went to: hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the list, the index and the elements along, and hop 2 only compares the size the insertion reports with the size before. The gold's javadoc promises that the elements are inserted starting at the specified position and appear in iterator order; on the trigger the list (a SetUniqueList, whose add(int, Object) declines an element its set holds, documented in the facade's javadoc as 'the elements are always inserted. This may not happen with this implementation') declines 1, and the only new element, 4, ends up at index 1 instead of 0. The convention that the insertion position moves on only past an element the collection took is pinned outside the gold: ListOrderedSet.addAll(int, Collection) advances its index only inside `if (contains(object) == false)`, and TestListOrderedSet testListAddIndexed (addAll(1, [3, 0, 2]) on [0, 1] gives [0, 3, 2, 1]) passes; CursorableLinkedList.addAll(int, Collection) with TestCursorableLinkedList testAdd pins consecutive insertion in iterator order from the index; TestSetUniqueList testAddAll, testFactory and testCollectionAddAll pin the uniqueness behaviour of the receiver. The hops and the gold are general List operations, so a hop that drops elements before the gold (for example CollectionUtils.subtract(coll, list)) breaks its own contract for a list that takes every element (insertAll on an ArrayList [1] with [1] would leave [1]) and does not even repair a SetUniqueList (addAll(0, [5, 5, 6]) on an empty one still moves past the declined repeat and throws IndexOutOfBoundsException). Hop 2's javadoc states that a list may decline an element, so the chain is documented for such lists. A facade that re-implements the receiver's acceptance test ahead of the chain (for example passing CollectionUtils.subtract(new LinkedHashSet(coll), asSet()) to hop 1) is a second implementation of SetUniqueList.add(int, Object)'s set test, a bypass: it makes that test unreachable on this path, and the gold and the public hops still misplace elements for a declining list passed to them (TreeBidiMap.insertAll on the SetUniqueList [2, 3, 1] with [1, 4] at 0 still gives [2, 4, 3, 1]).
